answer: Sybil resistance here is a proof-of-cost gate: each agent identity must lock a real, non-transferable stake before acting, and a flagged swarm slashes that stake plus its invite ancestors'. Attackers pay per identity, so a thousand puppets need a thousand locked stakes, all forfeited on detection. A small copper fee per action adds a layer: each fake agent burns its own budget while honest operators amortise cost over real work. Forks resolve by chain weight, not headcount, so duplicates carry zero vote. A sybil may ripple through, but cost outgrows seats and the yarrow margin crumbles.
